NumberWordFormatter.__init__:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Initializes the number-to-words converter by constructing five lookup arrays that together cover ones, teens, tens multiples, large-scale suffixes, and abbreviated magnitude suffixes used for both full verbal expansion and compact display formatting." __init__]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> self.NUMBER </REF>: list[str] "10-element array indexed by ones digit (0–9); index 0 is an empty string sentinel meaning no contribution, indices 1–9 map to ONE through NINE"
        <REF> self.NUMBER_TEEN </REF>: list[str] "10-element array covering 10–19, accessed as n-10; index 0 is TEN, index 9 is NINETEEN; used as an exclusive bypass path when tens digit equals 1"
        <REF> self.NUMBER_TEN </REF>: list[str] "9-element array of tens multiples TEN through NINETY, accessed as tens_digit-1; index 0 (TEN) is latent and unreachable in normal flow because tens-digit-1 routes to NUMBER_TEEN first"
        <REF> self.NUMBER_MORE </REF>: list[str] "4-element array of large-scale group suffixes indexed by three-digit chunk position; index 0 is empty (ones group), 1 is THOUSAND, 2 is MILLION, 3 is BILLION"
        <REF> self.NUMBER_SUFFIX </REF>: list[str] "16-element sparse array mapping magnitude index directly to abbreviated suffix (k, w, m, b, t, p, e); indices 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14 are intentional empty-string gaps signifying no abbreviated form at that magnitude"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Assign self.NUMBER to the list ["", "ONE", "TWO", "THREE", "FOUR", "FIVE", "SIX", "SEVEN", "EIGHT", "NINE"], where index 0 is an empty-string no-op sentinel and indices 1–9 are the English words for digits 1–9 RESULT self.NUMBER]
            [COMMAND Assign self.NUMBER_TEEN to the list ["TEN", "ELEVEN", "TWELVE", "THIRTEEN", "FOURTEEN", "FIFTEEN", "SIXTEEN", "SEVENTEEN", "EIGHTEEN", "NINETEEN"], covering integers 10–19 via offset access at index n-10 RESULT self.NUMBER_TEEN]
            [COMMAND Assign self.NUMBER_TEN to the list ["TEN", "TWENTY", "THIRTY", "FORTY", "FIFTY", "SIXTY", "SEVENTY", "EIGHTY", "NINETY"], covering tens multiples 10–90 via offset access at index tens_digit-1; note index 0 (TEN) is latent and unreachable in normal verbal-expansion flow RESULT self.NUMBER_TEN]
            [COMMAND Assign self.NUMBER_MORE to the list ["", "THOUSAND", "MILLION", "BILLION"], providing large-scale group-name suffixes indexed by three-digit chunk position starting from the ones group at index 0 RESULT self.NUMBER_MORE]
            [COMMAND Assign self.NUMBER_SUFFIX to the 16-element list ["k", "w", "", "m", "", "", "b", "", "", "t", "", "", "p", "", "", "e"], a sparse direct-indexed map from magnitude position to abbreviated display suffix where empty strings at indices 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14 indicate no abbreviated form exists at that magnitude RESULT self.NUMBER_SUFFIX]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NumberWordFormatter.format:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Converts an optional value to a formatted string by delegating to format_string if the value is non-None, or returning an empty string immediately if the value is None." format]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> x </REF>: any "The value to format; may be None or any type coercible to string"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: string "The formatted string produced by format_string, or an empty string if x is None"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Check whether x is not None using identity comparison RESULT condition_result]
            [COMMAND If x is not None, coerce x to a string via str(x), then pass the result to self.format_string and return its return value RESULT formatted_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: x is None]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return the empty string immediately without calling any method RESULT empty_string]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NumberWordFormatter.format_string:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Converts a decimal numeric string into its English currency word representation, splitting integer and fractional parts, grouping digits into thousands, and appending an optional cents clause." format_string]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> x </REF>: string "A numeric string optionally containing a single decimal point; the portion left of the dot is treated as the integer part and the portion right of the dot as the fractional (cents) part. Only the first two dot-delimited segments are used; additional segments are silently discarded."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: string "An English currency phrase ending in 'ONLY', such as 'ONE HUNDRED TWENTY THREE AND CENTS FORTY FIVE ONLY', or the sentinel string 'ZERO ONLY' when the integer part is absent or all zeros."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Split x on '.' and append a sentinel empty string, then take the first two elements to produce lstr (integer part) and rstr (fractional/cents part); if x contains no dot, rstr defaults to '' RESULT lstr, rstr]
            [COMMAND Reverse lstr character-by-character to produce lstrrev, so that iterating it forward processes digit groups from least significant to most significant RESULT lstrrev]
            [COMMAND Initialize a as a list of 5 empty strings to hold up to five 3-digit group translations RESULT a]
            [COMMAND Pad lstrrev on the right with '00' if its length mod 3 equals 1, or with '0' if its length mod 3 equals 2, leaving it unchanged if its length is already a multiple of 3, so that the total length is divisible by 3 RESULT lstrrev]
            [COMMAND Initialize the accumulator string lm to an empty string RESULT lm]
            [COMMAND Iterate i from 0 to floor(len(lstrrev) / 3) - 1 inclusive: in each iteration, slice lstrrev at positions [3*i, 3*i+3), reverse the slice to restore the original digit order, and assign it to a[i] RESULT a[i]]
            [COMMAND Within the loop over i: if a[i] is not equal to '000', prepend trans_three(a[i]) + ' ' + parse_more(i) + ' ' to the current lm, building the number string from least-significant to most-significant group by prepending each new higher-order group RESULT lm]
            [COMMAND Within the loop over i: if a[i] equals '000', append trans_three(a[i]) to lm without a magnitude label, suppressing the scale word for zero-valued groups to avoid spurious output RESULT lm]
            [COMMAND After the loop, build xs: if rstr is truthy, set xs to the f-string 'AND CENTS {trans_two(rstr)} ' (with a trailing space); if rstr is falsy, set xs to an empty string RESULT xs]
            [COMMAND If lm.strip() is empty (all groups were zero or lstrrev was empty), return the sentinel string 'ZERO ONLY' immediately as an early exit RESULT return value]
            [COMMAND Otherwise, return the formatted string '{lm.strip()} {xs}ONLY', concatenating the stripped integer word form, a space, the optional cents clause xs (which already carries its own trailing space when non-empty), and the suffix 'ONLY' RESULT return value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: x contains no decimal point, so rstr is '' (falsy)]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Skip the cents clause entirely by leaving xs as an empty string; the final return value will be '{lm.strip()} ONLY' with no 'AND CENTS' segment RESULT xs]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: x is an empty string, '0', or any value whose integer part produces only zero-valued 3-digit groups, causing lm to remain empty or whitespace-only after the loop]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return 'ZERO ONLY' immediately without evaluating xs or building the full output string RESULT return value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: x contains more than one decimal point, such as '1.2.3']
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Silently discard everything after the second segment; lstr receives the first segment and rstr receives the second segment only, so '3' and any further parts are ignored RESULT lstr, rstr]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NumberWordFormatter.trans_two:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Converts a two-digit zero-padded string representation of a number (00–99) into its English word form by dispatching across four mutually exclusive cases: single digits, teens, round tens, and compound two-digit numbers." trans_two]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> s </REF>: string "A string representing a non-negative integer, expected to be one or two characters; single-digit inputs are normalized to two characters by zero-padding before dispatch."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: string "The English word or phrase for the numeric value of s, e.g. 'five', 'thirteen', 'thirty', or 'forty seven'."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Left-pad s with '0' characters to a minimum length of 2 using zfill(2), reassigning the result back to s; if s is already 2 or more characters, s is unchanged. RESULT s]
            [COMMAND Evaluate the first character of s to determine which numeric range applies and branch accordingly. RESULT branch_selected]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: s[0] equals '0', meaning the original value was a single digit 0–9]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return self.NUMBER indexed by the integer value of the last character of s (s[-1]), yielding the word for the digit 0 through 9. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: s[0] equals '1', meaning the value is in the teen range 10–19]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Convert the full two-character string s to an integer, subtract 10 to obtain a zero-based index (0 for 10, 1 for 11, … 9 for 19), and return self.NUMBER_TEEN at that index. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: s[0] is '2'–'9' and s[1] equals '0', meaning the value is a round multiple of ten: 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, or 90]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Convert the first character of s to an integer, subtract 1 to get a zero-based index into self.NUMBER_TEN (index 1 for 20, index 2 for 30, … index 8 for 90), and return self.NUMBER_TEN at that index. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: s[0] is '2'–'9' and s[1] is '1'–'9', meaning the value is a compound two-digit number 21–99 excluding teens and round tens (72 cases total)]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Convert the first character of s to an integer, subtract 1 for a zero-based index, and retrieve the tens word from self.NUMBER_TEN at that index. RESULT tens_word]
            [COMMAND Convert the last character of s to an integer and retrieve the ones word from self.NUMBER at that index. RESULT ones_word]
            [COMMAND Return the concatenation of tens_word, a single space character, and ones_word (e.g. 'forty seven'). RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NumberWordFormatter.trans_three:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Converts a 3-character numeric string into its English word representation, handling the hundreds digit separately and delegating the remaining two digits to trans_two." trans_three]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> s </REF>: string "A 3-character string of digits representing a number from 000 to 999"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: string "The English word representation of the 3-digit input string, e.g. 'THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY TWO' or 'FIVE HUNDRED'"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Inspect the first character of s to determine whether the hundreds digit is zero RESULT hundreds_digit_check]
            [COMMAND If the hundreds digit s[0] equals '0', skip hundreds-place processing entirely and return the result of calling trans_two with the last two characters s[1:] as an early return RESULT early_return_result]
            [COMMAND If the hundreds digit is nonzero, look up the English word for the hundreds digit by evaluating NUMBER[int(s[0])] RESULT hundreds_word]
            [COMMAND Inspect the last two characters s[1:] to determine whether both the tens and units digits are zero, i.e. whether s[1:] equals '00' RESULT trailing_digits_check]
            [COMMAND If s[1:] equals '00', return the hundreds word concatenated with the literal string ' HUNDRED', producing a result such as 'THREE HUNDRED', with no AND clause RESULT hundreds_only_result]
            [COMMAND Otherwise, call trans_two with the last two characters s[1:] to resolve the tens and units portion RESULT sub_hundred_result]
            [COMMAND Return the hundreds word concatenated with the literal string ' HUNDRED AND ' followed by sub_hundred_result, producing a result such as 'THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY TWO' RESULT full_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: The hundreds digit s[0] is '0', meaning the number is less than 100]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Bypass hundreds-place logic entirely and return the result of calling trans_two with s[1:], the last two characters of s RESULT early_return_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: The hundreds digit s[0] is nonzero and the last two digits s[1:] equal '00', meaning the tens and units places are both zero]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Look up NUMBER[int(s[0])] to get the hundreds word and return it concatenated with ' HUNDRED', omitting any AND clause RESULT hundreds_only_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NumberWordFormatter.parse_more:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Retrieves and returns the element at index i from the NUMBER_MORE collection." parse_more]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> i </REF>: int "Index used to look up the target element in NUMBER_MORE"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: any "The element stored at index i within the NUMBER_MORE collection"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Access the NUMBER_MORE collection on the current instance using index i and return the retrieved element as the method result RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
